tasks.title: Academic Discussion
tasks.instruction:
Your professor is teaching a class. Write a post responding to the professor's question.
In your response, you should do the following:
• Express and support your personal opinion.
• Make a contribution to the discussion in your own words.
An effective response will contain at least 100 words.

professor.name: Dr. Achebe
professor.text: Volunteering is often defined as the act of offering time and labor to help others without receiving anything in return. In reality, however, volunteers are sometimes compensated for their work. For example, they may receive a small payment, a gift, or a free meal. These practices raise questions about the meaning of volunteering. In your opinion, is it appropriate to compensate people for volunteering? If so, in which situations is it appropriate? Please explain your thoughts.

posts.name: Kelly
posts.text: I do not think volunteers should receive any form of compensation because it can change the true meaning of volunteering. Volunteering should be about helping others, not earning rewards. Even small rewards may result in attracting people who are not truly motivated to help the cause.

posts.name: Paul
posts.text: It is appropriate to compensate volunteers when the work is difficult or requires a lot of time. This kind of compensation can increase participation. Small payments or rewards can motivate more people to help, especially in situations where the tasks are demanding.
